data.body:
# Readout + verdict: the `undecomposed` hard-override axis

**Verdict: RETUNE.** Not "keep as-is" and not "retire". The axis's low fire rate is real and its fires
are genuine, but its stated justification for grading conservatively is factually wrong on this corpus,
and its grade to floor mapping is miscalibrated in exactly the way `ac_unverifiable` and
`divergent_implementation` already were before their retunes. Follow-up story filed and linked (see
Outcome).

## Method (ADR 0054 compliant)

**Instrument: the persisted sidecar corpus, replayed read-only. Zero marginal LLM cost — no purpose-built
eval suite and no bulk re-review sweep.** The corpus is the `*-REVIEW_RESULT.json` gate-sidecar event
stream under `.tickets-tracker/<ticket-id>/` (the same stream `src/rebar/metrics/sidecar_metrics.py`
reads). Each `plan_review_result_v2` record carries `impact_model_version`, a `coverage` block, and a
`findings` array whose entries carry `verification.severity_attributes` — including the seven plan
severity axes. Replay was a local `python3` script over those files that (a) tabulated the
`undecomposed` grade of every verified finding, (b) counted the `g5_undecomposed_vetoed` coverage key,
(c) counted `coverage.det.P5.children` per review, and (d) re-matched every finding's text against the
shipped suppressor regex `_G5_UNDECOMPOSED_RE` imported directly from
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_lint.py`. Working tree untouched: `git status --porcelain src/ tests/`
is clean for this ticket.

**Corpus reachable from this checkout:**

| model version | reviews | verified findings (with `severity_attributes`) |
|---|---|---|
| plan-v3 | 662 | 10,250 |
| plan-v4 | 1,338 | 11,773 |

## AC1a — the firing findings

`undecomposed` non-`none` grades:

| | plan-v3 | plan-v4 |
|---|---|---|
| fires | **11 / 10,250 = 0.107%** | **18 / 11,773 = 0.153%** |
| distinct finding ids | 10 | 17 |
| distinct tickets | 5 | 7 |
| grades | 4 low / 4 medium / 3 high | 12 low / 4 medium / 2 high |
| decisions | 3 block / 3 advisory / 5 dropped | 3 block / 7 advisory / 8 dropped |
| co-fired criterion | G5 on 8 of 11 (also E6, G3, G4) | G5 on 15 of 18 (also F1, E6, E2) |

plan-v3 firing finding ids: `f47d8825dca8374e6`, `fde95b0e8dea42a81`, `f87921b49997accf6` (all three on
ticket `58b0-104b-777c-4227`), `fa3e05ad36732bda2` (`1aa8-cdde-4ff6-40d0`), `f5218589457dd3a02`
(`5967-4476-7f9f-442d`), `f7865fab0878a68e4` + `f5cf9774b014413ac` (`62a3-a49d-04a0-4f18`),
`f9073502636fcc14f` + `fe03899cbf6f40740` + `f09050c2dfd6b2fbc` (`7c27-10fc-4fe6-4b56`, the last one
recorded on two successive reviews).

plan-v4 firing finding ids: `f1a0271d807f6e1d9`, `f7144fc781f6e3a77`, `f0b8b3171984030f6`,
`f88d8c5484c41928f`, `ffee545cc46314b05`, `f29222603c56e06b0` (all on `2127-348c-c41d-472e`),
`f26d530cb8944d783` (`3b5f-1b21-ee14-4bdf`), `fa102d52217733c57`, `f3aa2019272f5e1e2`,
`f8ef9c1c1b2a13af3`, `fc52ffa58eae1e193`, `f31d69922fd621333`, `f2d9d415ad2debc0a`
(`5200-e04e-246e-4aae`), `f22e0c44fb8ee3080` (`7be3-69af-6e84-4235`), `f0d3b6a0ff5ba4999`
(`a89d-4dd2-f421-417a`), `f6dfe0552a79c6e46` (`ad63-17ad-d545-45d4`), `f98c2bdea40065a4a`
(`b690-f232-5bae-4b8b`).

**Are they genuine?** Yes. Reading the finding text: they are almost all the "this ticket bundles N
independently valuable / independently releasable slices" class, plus one true decomposition-absence
case (`f47d8825dca8374e6`: "the plan's own AC calls for 5 child tickets but the store shows only 1
child recorded" — that one is store-grounded and blocked correctly). I found no obviously spurious fire.

**Was the floor load-bearing?** Overwhelmingly yes, and that is the problem.

- The `undecomposed` floor was the **only** hard override present in **25 of the 29** fires (plan-v3
  8/11, plan-v4 17/18) — no `dod_uncertifiable`, no `broken_oracle`/`missing_oracle`, no
  `contradicts_reality`/`omits_required_site`.
- Recomputing `impact_plan` with `undecomposed` forced to `none` (using the shipped `_SEV01`,
  `ORACLE_GRADE01`, `DIVERGENCE_GRADE01` tables and the documented composition) gives **0.0** for most
  of those findings. Without the axis they would carry no impact at all.
- Concretely: `f6dfe0552a79c6e46` (ticket `ad63-17ad-d545-45d4`) was graded **`low`**, and the floor
  alone took it to impact 0.85; at validity 0.7143 that is priority 0.6072 against a 0.60 block line —
  a **BLOCK produced entirely by a `low` grade**. Its impact without the axis is 0.0.

## AC1b — the measured G5 suppression rate

**0.00%. The G5 deterministic veto fired zero times in 2,000 recorded plan-v3 + plan-v4 reviews.**

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` writes `coverage["g5_undecomposed_vetoed"] = len(vetoed_g5)` only
when the veto actually dropped something. That key is **absent from every one of the 2,000 sidecars** —
0 reviews with a veto, 0 findings suppressed.

It is also barely applicable. `veto_undecomposed_g5` is a no-op when the ticket has no children, and
`coverage.det.P5.children` shows the reviewed population is overwhelmingly childless:

| | tickets with children | childless |
|---|---|---|
| plan-v3 | 61 (9.3%) | 596 |
| plan-v4 | 115 (8.6%) | 1,223 |

So the ticket's explanation (1) — "most reviewed tickets do have children, G5 correctly suppresses the
false flat findings, 0.07% is the correct residual" — is **contradicted on both halves**: over 90% of
reviewed tickets are childless (the veto cannot apply), and on the <10% where it could apply it never
once did.

## AC1c — the inverse population

Match rule: the shipped `_G5_UNDECOMPOSED_RE` from `det_lint.py`, applied case-insensitively to each
finding's `finding` + `impact` + `suggested_fix` text (the same fields `_is_undecomposed_claim` scans).

- plan-v3: **33** findings text-match but scored `undecomposed` = `none`.
- plan-v4: **17** findings text-match but scored `undecomposed` = `none`.

Inspecting a 12-per-version sample, these are **regex false positives, not missed flat-plan defects**.
They are findings about *code* decomposition and *module* seams whose prose happens to contain
"should be split" / "break down" — e.g. `f4519a0fd25bea14d` and `ff7283fc9b80058de` ("the call-graph
seam along which `gate_dispatch.py` should be split is not named"), `f29b2991c1207b328` (the 800-LOC
module-size cap), `f04205f3aaf43fcb1` (a shared helper's return type). None describes a flat *plan*.

So there is **no evidence of a large missed class** analogous to the ~90%-missed divergence class that
motivated plan-v4. Explanation (2) in its strong form ("a real class of flat-plan defects is scoring
0.0") is **not supported**.

## AC2 — which explanation the evidence supports, and the outcome

**Neither cleanly — a third reading fits the data, and it is a calibration defect rather than a
detection one.**

- Against explanation (1): the suppressor cited as the reason for the low rate is **inert** (0 fires)
  and inapplicable to 90%+ of the population. The residual is not "correctly suppressed"; nothing was
  suppressed.
- Against explanation (2): the axis is **not unreachable**. It fires on 5 plan-v3 and 7 plan-v4 tickets,
  its rate is stable and slightly *higher* under plan-v4 (0.107% to 0.153%), 6 of 29 fires blocked, and
  the inverse population is text noise rather than missed defects. There is no dark class to recover.
- What the evidence does show: **the hedge in the axis text points at a suppressor that does not exist
  in practice**, and **the grade to floor mapping is broken**. Any non-`none` grade floors to 0.85
  (`review_kernel/decide.py`), so `low` == `high`. 16 of the 29 fires were `low`; in 25 of 29 the floor
  was the sole override; and at least one `low` grade blocked a plan on the floor alone. This is
  precisely the miscalibration already fixed for `ac_unverifiable` (ORACLE_GRADE01, plan-v3, where 56%
  of floor-driven blocks only wanted a more specific command) and for `divergent_implementation`
  (DIVERGENCE_GRADE01, plan-v4). `undecomposed` is the **last ordinal-ladder hard-override axis still
  flooring on its weakest grade.**

**Outcome (b): follow-up story linked.** `d4c2-b67e-ab99-4410` / `fixable-angular-caribou` — "Retune the
'undecomposed' hard-override axis: gate the 0.85 floor on grade, drop the inert-G5 hedge from its prompt
text" — linked to this ticket with `discovered_from`. It scopes: (i) gate the hard override on grade
(floor only medium|high, or convert to a closed kind set where "bundles N slices" contributes below every
block threshold), (ii) rewrite the axis text in `plan_review_verifier.md`,
`plan_review_verifier_agentic.md` and `verify_models.py` to stop citing the inert suppressor, and
(iii) decide separately whether `veto_undecomposed_g5` earns its keep at 0 measured fires. The story
records that any impact-model shape change costs an IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump closing the plan-v4 cohort
and must be batched per ADR 0054 section 4.

## Limits — what I verified vs what I could not observe

Verified directly from this checkout:

- Every count above (fires, grades, decisions, criteria, child counts, G5 veto key, inverse matches) is
  a replay over the `.tickets-tracker/*/*REVIEW_RESULT.json` sidecars present here. Reproducible.
- The source facts: the seven axes and `_PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_AXES` + `_PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_FLOOR = 0.85`
  in `review_kernel/decide.py`; the axis field description in `review_kernel/verify_models.py`; the
  identical hedge in both reviewer prompts; the veto and its regex in `plan_review/det_lint.py`; the
  post-Pass-1 seam and the conditional coverage write in `plan_review/pass1.py`.

Could NOT observe:

1. **The exact 18,085-finding denominator is not reachable from this checkout.** What is here is 10,250
   verified plan-v3 findings across 662 reviews — a subset. My plan-v3 rate is **11/10,250 = 0.107%**
   against the ticket's cited **12/18,085 = 0.07%**. Same order of magnitude, same two-orders-below-
   every-other-axis conclusion, but the numbers are **not** the ticket's numbers and I did not attempt
   to reconcile them. I have not reproduced the seven-axis comparison table in the ticket description
   either — only the `undecomposed` column.
2. **The upstream suppressor is unmeasurable from this instrument.** `decomposition_state_block()`
   injects an authoritative "do NOT flag this ticket as flat/undecomposed" context block into the G5
   finder *before* any finding exists. Nothing about that injection is recorded in the sidecar, so I can
   only prove the **post-Pass-1 veto** never fired. I cannot rule out that the injected block prevents
   findings from ever being emitted. That caveat is bounded, though: the block is also empty when the
   ticket has no children, and 90%+ of reviewed tickets are childless.
3. **1,217 plan-v3 findings (10.6%) and 2,328 plan-v4 findings carry no `verification` block** (DET-tier
   or unverified) and are excluded from every rate above. Rates are over verified findings only.
4. **The inverse-population judgement is a sample, not a census.** I read 12 matches per model version
   out of 33 / 17, not all 50. The counts are exact; the "these are regex false positives" reading rests
   on that sample.
5. **The counterfactual impact figures are a re-implementation.** I recomputed `impact_plan` with
   `undecomposed` forced to `none` by importing the shipped `_SEV01` / `ORACLE_GRADE01` /
   `DIVERGENCE_GRADE01` tables and mirroring the documented MAX to amplifier to floor composition, rather
   than calling the shipped function. The "sole override" count (25/29) is a direct read of the recorded
   attributes and does not depend on that re-implementation.
6. **Fires are not deduplicated by ticket in the headline rate.** 29 fires collapse to 27 distinct
   finding ids across 12 distinct tickets, because re-reviews of the same ticket re-record the same
   finding. The per-finding rate is the honest one for an axis-calibration question, but the
   distinct-ticket count is the better read of how much real-world work the axis touched.
